# resolve_link { #labdata.gitutil.resolve_link }

```python
labdata.gitutil.resolve_link(repo, path, target)
```

Locate the file a committed symbolic link points at.

A relative target is resolved against the directory the link sits in, which
is how the filesystem reads it. A target may leave the repository, by
climbing out with ``..`` or by being absolute: publishing is opt-in through
the manifest, so what a link reaches is something the repository said out
loud, and a result written to scratch space outside the working tree is a
normal thing to publish.

## Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

<code>[**repo**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[Union](`typing.Union`)\[[Location](`labdata.location.Location`), [Path](`pathlib.Path`), [str](`str`)\]]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   Working tree holding the link, on this machine or another.

<code>[**path**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[str](`str`)]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   Repository-relative path of the link itself.

<code>[**target**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[str](`str`)]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   Target as committed, from [](`labdata.gitutil.link_target`).

## Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

<code>[]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[Optional](`typing.Optional`)\[[Location](`labdata.location.Location`)\]]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   Location of the file, or `None` when nothing is there. A link resolves on the machine its repository is on, so a target read over ssh is looked for on the far side.
